objective_text: State the characteristics shared by all living organisms and explain each one using a named example.
Explain why the binomial system is used and describe the hierarchical classification of organisms.
Describe the main features of the five kingdoms and give an example organism from each.
Describe the features used to classify vertebrates into their five groups and invertebrates into their major groups.
Construct and use a dichotomous key to identify an unknown organism.
Identify the structures of animal and plant cells and state the function of each structure.
Explain how the shape of a specialised cell is adapted to carry out its function.
Describe the levels of organisation from cell to organ system and give an example of each level.
Calculate the magnification of a drawing and the actual size of a specimen using the magnification equation.
Describe how organ systems work together in a mammal, using the digestive and transport systems as examples.
Define diffusion and describe the factors that affect the rate of diffusion across a membrane.
Define osmosis and predict the effect of solutions of different concentrations on plant and animal cells.
Describe active transport and explain why it is needed in root hair cells and in the gut.
Explain the importance of surface area to volume ratio for the exchange of substances in organisms.
Describe experiments that investigate diffusion and osmosis and interpret the results.
